title: Human-Centered AI
tagline: AI that makes people better, not obsolete
summary: The question isn't 'what can AI replace?' It's 'what can AI unlock in people who were previously limited?' Human-centered AI design starts with a deep understanding of human needs, not with technology capabilities. The best AI systems are the ones people barely notice because they work so naturally.

pillars.name: Augment, Don't Replace
pillars.description: Design AI systems that make your people more capable, not fewer. The goal is to remove the tedious and expand the creative — to let humans do more of what only humans can do.

pillars.name: Trust Through Transparency
pillars.description: People adopt AI faster when they understand it. Design systems that explain themselves, surface their confidence levels, and make it easy to verify outputs. Opaque AI creates resistance.

pillars.name: Feedback Loops
pillars.description: Build in mechanisms for people to correct, improve, and guide the AI. The best AI systems get better over time because they incorporate human judgment, not despite it.

pillars.name: Inclusive Design
pillars.description: Design for the full range of users — different technical comfort levels, languages, abilities, and contexts. AI that only works for power users has a short lifetime.

keyQuestions: What does this person actually need to accomplish — and does the AI help them get there faster?
Where does this AI take control away from the user, and is that the right trade-off?
How does someone correct the AI when it's wrong?
Who isn't represented in our design assumptions, and how does that create risk?
exampleInPractice: When designing the VoicePath patient intake agent, we ran sessions with actual healthcare admin staff — not executives. Their feedback reshaped the entire interaction model. The version they helped design had 50% faster adoption than the first prototype. [NEEDS REVIEW BY MARLON]
